titulo: Regular pretérito indefinido: The indefinido of -ar verbs

aula.objetivo: Narrate what happened and is already finished («ayer», «anoche», «el año pasado») with the regular -ar, -er and -ir forms of the pretérito indefinido, get the accent marks right («hablé», «habló»), handle the spelling changes («busqué», «llegué», «empecé», «leyó»), and tell the indefinido apart from the pretérito perfecto.

blocos.texto: You're arriving at A2 already able to introduce yourself, talk about your family, order at a café, tell the time, ask for directions, narrate your routine, say what you like, and say what you've done today with the pretérito perfecto. At this level you start telling stories: what happened yesterday, last week, on vacation. The first tense you need is the pretérito indefinido, the tense for finished facts. English's simple past («I talked», «she talked») never changes shape for person, so this is genuinely new ground: Spanish has six distinct endings, and it's worth paying close attention to both the endings themselves and the accent marks that tell subjects apart.

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: use the pretérito indefinido for something that happened and ended at a moment you can name: «ayer», «anoche», «el lunes», «en 2019», «hace dos días». STEP 2: for -ar verbs, drop the «-ar» from the infinitive and add these endings: -é, -aste, -ó, -amos, -asteis, -aron. «Hablar» becomes «hablé, hablaste, habló, hablamos, hablasteis, hablaron». STEP 3: the first person (yo) and the third person (él, ella, usted) carry a written accent: «hablé» and «habló». The accent marks the stressed syllable and also keeps the past apart from the present: «hablo» (I speak) versus «habló» (he/she spoke). STEP 4: in «nosotros», the indefinido of -ar verbs looks exactly like the present: «hablamos». Context settles it: «Ayer hablamos» is past, «Hablamos cada día» is a habit. STEP 5: «vosotros» (Spain) ends in «-asteis»: «hablasteis». In Latin America, «ustedes» uses «hablaron». STEP 6: the subject pronoun is almost always dropped, because the ending already says who it is: «Ayer cené en casa» (I had dinner at home yesterday). STEP 7: the indefinido has no connection to the present — the fact is closed off in the past. With «hoy», «esta semana» or «este año», which haven't ended yet, Spain prefers the pretérito perfecto from lesson 17: «Hoy he trabajado mucho». In much of Latin America people say «Hoy trabajé mucho» instead, since there the indefinido often takes over the perfecto's job.
blocos.comparacao: English's simple past («I talked», «you talked», «he talked») never changes shape for the subject at all, so the whole idea of six distinct person-endings is new ground, not something to carry over. The trickiest traps here are specific to Spanish spelling: the «-ó» ending (with no English equivalent at all), the «-aron» plural ending, and the «vosotros» form «hablasteis», which has no counterpart in English either since English marks no distinction between «you» singular and «you» plural. The written accent is another new habit: English never marks stress with an accent mark, but in Spanish it's what tells «hablo» (I speak, present) apart from «habló» (he/she spoke, past).

exemplos.ru: El año pasado viajé a Valencia.
exemplos.pt: Last year I traveled to Valencia.

exemplos.ru: Anoche cenamos en casa de Marta.
exemplos.pt: Last night we had dinner at Marta's place.

erros.motivo: With «ayer», the fact is finished: use the indefinido, not the present.
With «tú», the ending is «-aste», with no final «s».
Without the accent, «hable» is a different verb form; the «yo» indefinido takes «-é».

blocos.enunciado: Say out loud what you did yesterday using five -ar verbs: «Ayer trabajé… Ayer hablé… Ayer compré… Anoche cené… Ayer caminé…» Then say what a friend did, using the «él, ella» form.
